name: Electrocaloric cold cap
subtitle: a thin cap that saves hair during chemotherapy

effects.effect: a plastic film cools when an electric field across it is switched off

effect: a plastic film cools when an electric field across it is switched off
how: Hair loss makes many cancer patients dread chemotherapy, and chilling the scalp during treatment saves the hair, but today's cold caps are tethered to a fridge pumping coolant. This cap is lined with thin plastic films that warm when a voltage is switched on and cool when it is switched off; cycled in step, they pump heat from the scalp to the cap's outer skin on battery power, so patients can move about or be treated at home.
obstacle: Today's films pump only a little heat, and a cap must pull away tens of watts for several hours.
why: Portable scalp cooling could make more patients accept life-saving chemotherapy.
real: Electrocaloric polymer heat pumps exist only as benchtop devices (Berkeley Lab/UCLA 2025) and scalp cooling uses gel or chiller caps; no electrocaloric wearable or cold cap found.
